title: Quantification of Blumenol Derivatives as Leaf Biomarkers for Plant-AMF Association
author: Elisabeth Mindt
license_note: PMC full-text XML — Bio-protocol — CC-BY confirmed in article XML

steps.title: Harvest and freeze leaf tissue
steps.instruction: Harvest leaves, immediately freeze in liquid nitrogen using stainless steel tweezers, and store at –80 °C until processing.

steps.title: Grind frozen leaf under liquid nitrogen
steps.instruction: Grind the frozen leaf material in a pre‑chilled mortar and pestle while maintaining liquid‑nitrogen temperature.

steps.title: Aliquot leaf into pre‑cooled tubes
steps.instruction: Aliquot approximately 100 mg of frozen leaf into pre‑cooled, pre‑weighed 96‑well BioTube™ racks (or 2 ml Eppendorf tubes) each containing two steel balls (Ø 3 mm for BioTubes, Ø 4 mm for Eppendorf). Record the exact mass and keep samples on liquid nitrogen or at –80 °C.

steps.title: Prepare extraction buffer with internal standard
steps.instruction: Prepare extraction buffer with D₆‑ABA: mix 200 ml MilliQ H₂O, 800 ml LC‑grade MeOH, and 1.25 ml of 10 ng µl⁻¹ D₆‑ABA (final concentration 10 ng per 800 µl buffer). Keep the buffer ice‑cold.

steps.title: Add extraction buffer and seal
steps.instruction: Add 800 µl ice‑cold extraction buffer to each tube using an 8‑channel pipette, replace the caps with a rubber sealing mat, and keep the tubes on ice.

steps.title: Homogenize samples in Geno/Grinder
steps.instruction: Homogenize the samples in a Geno/Grinder® for 60 s at 1,000 strokes min⁻¹ (Geno/Grinder 2000 setting: 1× at 000).

steps.title: Centrifuge and collect supernatant
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 2,000 × g for 20 min at 4 °C. Transfer the supernatant to a new 96‑well BioTube rack or Eppendorf tube without steel balls and centrifuge again under the same conditions.

steps.title: Transfer aliquots for LC‑MS analysis
steps.instruction: Transfer 100 µl of the supernatant to skirted 96‑well microplates and seal wells with LC‑MS‑compatible sealing film for immediate analysis.

steps.title: Prepare freezer backup aliquots
steps.instruction: Transfer 190 µl of the supernatant to a 96‑well PCR plate and seal with domed 8‑strip caps for freezer backup. If Eppendorf tubes were used, transfer 700 µl to 1.5 ml screw‑neck vials for storage.

steps.title: Create mixed quality control sample
steps.instruction: Prepare a mixed QC sample for each plate by combining 10 µl from each sample into a 1.5 ml screw‑neck vial; use extraction buffer as blank for background calculations.

steps.title: Set up UHPLC gradient and conditions
steps.instruction: Use an Agilent ZORBAX Eclipse XDB‑C18 column. Mobile phase A = 0.1 % (v/v) acetonitrile + 0.05 % (v/v) formic acid in MilliQ H₂O; mobile phase B = 100 % methanol. Apply the gradient shown in Table 1, flow rate 0.5 ml min⁻¹, column temperature 42 °C, sample‑tray temperature 10 °C, injection volume 5 µl.

steps.title: Configure HESI source and MS parameters
steps.instruction: Set the Bruker EVO‑Q Elite triple quadrupole MS HESI source to: spray voltage ±4,500 V, cone temperature 350 °C, probe temperature 300 °C, cone gas flow 35, nebulizer gas flow 60, probe gas flow 55.

steps.title: Run MRM detection for blumenol derivatives
steps.instruction: Inject standards (Roseoside, Corchoionoside C, Blumenol C glucoside, Byzantionoside B) to verify system performance. Perform multiple‑reaction monitoring using the quantifier and qualifier m/z values and collision energies listed in Table 2, with a 1 min recording window at the expected retention time for each compound.

steps.title: Perform QC checks during batch run
steps.instruction: Analyze the mixed QC sample after every 15–20 analytical samples; compare QC runs to monitor instrument performance, retention‑time shifts, and mass‑spectrometer sensitivity changes.
